children: Stock futures were edging higher on Wednesday as oil prices held steady at below $100 a barrel, even after President Donald Trump threatened to "annihilate" Iran.
Chip and memory stocks slipped as investors locked in some profit from the previous session's rally. Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Qualcomm, and Sandisk all fell ahead of the opening bell.
Server makers were having a better time of it, suggesting investors are still bullish on AI. Super Micro Computer Inc. added 1.1% and Dell Technologies gained 0.9% in premarket trading.
IonQ surged 12% after the quantum platform and foundry said it had achieved a major breakthrough by developing and testing the first real-time quantum error correction decoder.

Six Flags climbed 1.1%. Activist Jana Partners is pushing the theme-park operator to explore a sale, The Wall Street Journal reported. Jana and Six Flags didn't respond to requests for comment from Barron's.
Mining stocks Freeport-McMoRan and Newmont fell 1.4% and 1.8%, respectively, as the price of gold extended its recent slump. Higher interest rates tend to drag down bullion and other precious metals.
